config.title: usePrevious

intro.title: usePrevious
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom Vue composable called `usePrevious` that tracks and returns the previous value of a reactive variable. You will learn how to use Vue's `ref` and `watch` to observe changes and store historical data. This involves core JavaScript concepts like state management and side effects. By the end, you'll understand how to create reusable logic for tracking previous values in your Vue applications.
intro.usecase: The usePrevious hook is essential in scenarios where you need to track changes between state updates. In dashboards, it helps detect when metric values cross thresholds to trigger alerts or visual highlights. In forms, it enables comparing current and previous input values to validate changes or show confirmation dialogs. This pattern is also valuable in interactive filters where you need to know what changed to optimize API calls or animate transitions.

objectives: Implement a custom usePrevious composable function in Vue
Initialize a ref to store the previous value of a reactive state
Apply the watch function to detect changes in a reactive value
Update the previous value ref when the current value changes
Integrate the usePrevious composable into a Vue component
Render both current and previous values in a component template
Manipulate reactive data to observe the usePrevious composable in action
